subject: Logging access, masking & retention — action summary and open asks
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Rao <anika@medlytix.com>, Tom Becker <tbecker@medlytix.com>, MedLytix Security Team <security@medlytix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Logging access, masking & retention — call recap and open asks

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to map the scope. Below is a concise recap and the concrete asks we discussed. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary from today's discovery call:
- Primary concern: protect patient-identifiable fields in request/response logs while keeping enough telemetry for debugging and fraud detection.
- Scope: API request/response payloads, headers, tracing identifiers (trace_id, session_id), and metadata that flow to our logging/observability pipeline.
- Data residency: production logs must remain in US regions only; no export to non-US without explicit approval.
- Retention: MedLytix initial ask = 90 days for request/response logs; longer retention for aggregated metrics ok.

Open asks we agreed Redwood will follow up on:
1) Redaction vs pseudonymization options: provide an action matrix showing tradeoffs (debuggability, reversibility, performance, cost).
2) Header inventory: identify which headers Redwood will redact by default and which can be pseudonymized.
3) Trace mapping: describe whether trace_id mapping to original values can be kept in a separate, customer-managed KV store (recommended) and how retrieval is controlled.
4) Retention controls: confirm retention enforcement points (edge / ingest / long-term store) and provide configuration knobs (TTL, sampling).
5) SOC2 / pen-test evidence: share relevant excerpts or certificates we can include in your compliance pack.
6) Timeline: deliver a preliminary redaction/pseudonymization matrix + sample logging schema by EOD Wed (2027-05-19).

Attachments: redwood-redaction-proposal-v1.xlsx (proposed matrix), sample-logging-schema.json (example event shape).

Next steps:
- Redwood: Ben will draft the matrix and technical approach; Chloe will own timeline and compliance artifacts.
- MedLytix: confirm that 90 days retention is acceptable, and list any headers that must remain intact for your downstream tooling by Tuesday.
- Follow-up: 30-minute technical sync tentatively scheduled for Thu 2027-05-20 (calendar invite to follow).

Thanks — feel free to reply inline with corrections.

Best,
Chloe Martin

From: Anika Rao <anika@medlytix.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Logging access, masking & retention — call recap and open asks

Thanks Chloe — that matches our notes. A couple of clarifying questions before you produce the matrix: 

1) Headers: we have several custom headers that carry patient reference IDs (X-ML-Patient-ID) and routing info (X-Proxy-Route). We need patient IDs removed from any plaintext logs. Is hashing at ingest acceptable, or do you require full redaction? If hashing, we need to understand salt management and whether the hash is reversible by Redwood.

2) Trace/session identifiers: we prefer pseudonymization so we can correlate events internally. Can Redwood support a customer-controlled mapping (e.g., an encrypted, customer-managed KV store or HSM) so you never hold a reversible mapping in plaintext?

3) Retention: 90 days is our target, but we may need 180 days for certain audit cases. Can you describe how retention policy enforcement works if a customer requests different TTLs per log type?

4) Access control: who at Redwood can access raw logs if unredacted? We need an explanation of RBAC, audit trails, and emergency access processes.

5) Evidence: can you share a redacted excerpt of the SOC2 report and any recent pen-test summary (redacted)? We will treat it as confidential.

I've attached our internal requirements doc: medlytix-logging-requirements-v2.docx.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Logging access, masking & retention — internal plan

Internal note / proposed plan (will share external version after your review):

Quick proposal we can send MedLytix that addresses their asks:
- Option A (Inline redaction): strip/replace PII at ingest. Pros: simplest, no reversible mapping stored. Cons: loses original payload for debugging. Suggested for headers and patient identifiers.
- Option B (Pseudonymization + guarded mapping): replace PII with deterministic pseudonyms and store mapping in a customer-owned, encrypted KV (we provide an integration pattern). Pros: preserves correlatability. Cons: increases retrieval latency and requires strict IAM + audit.
- Trace handling: always pseudonymize trace_id at edge; store a hashed trace fingerprint in logs for joinability. Provide optional customer-managed mapping for full original->pseudonym lookups audited via HSM.
- Retention: implement TTL in the hot log store with enforcement at ingestion + background purge in cold store. Support per-log-type TTLs via config flag (default 90d, up to 365d with compliance review).
- RBAC / Access: restrict raw log access to SRE/security engineers via Just-In-Time (JIT) access with recorded justification and one-click revoke. All accesses create audit entries and are retained 12 months.

Action items for us:
- I will assemble a technical appendix describing the edge/redaction pipeline and the KV integration pattern (target: EOD Wed 2027-05-19).
- Chloe: compile SOC2 excerpts and paste any compliance links.
- Lauren: add this to the deal playbook and update the HubSpot record (contact/attachment links).
